title: Passive with bli and -s
goal: Choose and form natural Bokmål passives with bli or -s.

objectives.statement: Choose and form natural Bokmål passives with bli or -s.
Omit an irrelevant agent and choose a natural s-passive or bli-passive pattern for routines, instructions, and events.

sections.title: A library gets ready to reopen

spans.value: The local library has been closed for repairs. On Monday morning, librarian Ingrid shows her colleague Marius what still needs to happen before the doors open.
Nesten. Lesesalen blir vasket i dag, og møterommet blir malt i morgen.

blocks.translation: Almost. The reading room is being cleaned today, and the meeting room will be painted tomorrow.

spans.value: De blir hengt opp etter lunsj.

blocks.translation: They will be put up after lunch.

spans.value: Og hvordan leverer folk bøker mens hoveddøra er stengt?

blocks.translation: And how do people return books while the main door is closed?

spans.value: Bøkene leveres i luka ved siden av inngangen.

blocks.translation: The books are returned through the hatch next to the entrance.

spans.value: Skal vi skrive hvem som tømmer luka?

blocks.translation: Should we write who empties the hatch?

spans.value: Nei, det er ikke viktig for publikum. Luka tømmes hver kveld.

blocks.translation: No, that is not important to the public. The hatch is emptied every evening.

spans.value: Greit. Da skriver jeg også at lånekort bestilles på nettet.

blocks.translation: All right. Then I’ll also write that library cards are ordered online.

spans.value: The dialogue describes actions without always naming the person who performs them. Readers need to know what happens to the library, rooms, signs, books, and hatch. They do not usually need to know which employee does each job.
Norwegian commonly uses two passive patterns here:

en.value: The reading room is being cleaned today.
The hatch is emptied every evening.

spans.value: Both sentences use the passive voice (passiv). In the passive patterns taught here, attention commonly falls on the affected thing or the event rather than the person performing the action.
The two passive patterns often describe similar situations, but they do not always present them in the same way.
commonly presents an action as an event: something happens to a person or thing. It is especially natural when discussing a particular job, change, or occurrence.

en.value: The reading room is being cleaned today.

no.value: Skiltene blir hengt opp etter lunsj.

en.value: The signs will be put up after lunch.

spans.value: is often natural for routines, general procedures, notices, schedules, and concise instructions.

en.value: The hatch is emptied every evening.
Library cards are ordered online.

items.value: when presenting a particular action or event.
when presenting a routine, procedure, instruction, or compact institutional statement.

spans.value: This is a strong practical tendency, not an absolute division. In some contexts, both forms are possible. The speaker’s choice affects what is foregrounded.

no.value: Døra åpnes hver morgen klokka ti.

en.value: The door is opened every morning at ten.

no.value: Døra blir åpnet i morgen klokka ti.

en.value: The door will be opened tomorrow at ten.

spans.value: The affected noun and action are the same.
For many verbs whose infinitive ends in

en.value: to wash → is washed / are washed
to open → is opened / are opened
to deliver or return → is delivered or returned

spans.value: You can also recognize the form by starting with the ordinary present tense, removing final

en.value: opens → is opened
orders → is ordered
empties → is emptied

spans.value: The s-passive does not change according to whether the affected noun is singular or plural:

en.value: The book is returned at the desk.
The books are returned at the desk.

spans.value: This pattern is common in public information because it is short and impersonal.

en.value: The doors are opened at ten.

no.value: Mat og drikke betales i kassen.

en.value: Food and drink are paid for at the till.
The form is submitted electronically.
Mobile phones are switched off before the meeting.

spans.value: The last sentence is formally a statement, but in context it functions as an instruction.
Common mistake: keeping the present-tense r
directly to a present-tense form ending in

en.value: Intended meaning: The doors are opened at ten.
The doors are opened at ten.

spans.value: The bli-passive uses a form of
followed by a past participle (perfektum partisipp):
for a present or anticipated event:

en.value: The floor is being washed now.
The package will be sent this afternoon.
The windows will be replaced next week.

spans.value: when the event happened in the past:

en.value: The floor was washed yesterday.
The package was sent on Friday.
The windows were replaced last year.
washed
opened
sent
written
done
put up

spans.value: carries the tense. The participle stays in its passive construction form:

en.value: The room is being painted.
The rooms are being painted.
The room was painted.

spans.value: Common mistake: using two passive markers

en.value: Intended meaning: The room is being painted.
The room is being painted.

spans.value: when the context calls for it:

en.value: The room is painted every three years.

spans.value: Now compare the two patterns more closely.

en.value: The newspapers are put out every morning.

spans.value: signals a repeated routine. The s-passive is concise and natural.

no.value: De nye avisstativene blir satt ut i morgen.

en.value: The new newspaper racks will be put out tomorrow.

spans.value: This is one planned event involving particular racks. The bli-passive foregrounds what will happen to them.

en.value: The receipt is checked at the exit.

spans.value: This tells customers what procedure to follow. It does not matter which employee checks the receipt.

en.value: The receipt was checked at the exit.
Email is answered within two working days.

no.value: Meldingen din blir besvart i morgen.

en.value: Your message will be answered tomorrow.

spans.value: The difference is not simply plural versus singular. A singular noun can occur in a routine:

en.value: The hatch is emptied every evening.

spans.value: A plural noun can occur in a particular event:

no.value: De nye skiltene blir hengt opp i dag.

en.value: The new signs will be put up today.

spans.value: Look instead at meaning and context. Routines and instructions often favor the s-passive, while particular occurrences often favor the bli-passive. However, an s-passive can also be natural for a particular scheduled occurrence in a schedule, notice, or compact institutional statement, as in
An active sentence names the person or group performing the action:

en.value: The cleaners are washing the reading room today.

spans.value: A passive sentence can omit that information:

en.value: The reading room is being cleaned today.

spans.value: The passive version is useful because the update concerns the room and the reopening plan. The identity of the cleaners adds little.

no.value: De ansatte tømmer luka hver kveld.

en.value: The employees empty the hatch every evening.
The hatch is emptied every evening.

spans.value: The second sentence is more suitable for a public notice. Visitors need the routine, not the staff assignment.
Do not remove a person merely because a passive is grammatically possible. Remove the agent when that person is unknown, obvious, or irrelevant to the message.

en.value: The municipality is closing the road on Monday.
The road will be closed on Monday.

spans.value: The active sentence may be useful when responsibility matters. The passive sentence is natural when road users mainly need to know what will happen.
Later that afternoon, Marius shows Ingrid the notice he has prepared.
Nå står det at hoveddøra blir åpnet på onsdag klokka ti.

blocks.translation: It now says that the main door will be opened at ten on Wednesday.

spans.value: Bra. Har du skrevet hva folk gjør med bøker før onsdag?

blocks.translation: Good. Have you written what people do with books before Wednesday?

spans.value: Ja. Bøkene leveres i luka, og luka tømmes hver kveld.

blocks.translation: Yes. Books are returned through the hatch, and the hatch is emptied every evening.
Great. What about the reading room?

spans.value: Den blir vasket i dag. De nye lampene blir montert i morgen.

blocks.translation: It is being cleaned today. The new lamps will be installed tomorrow.

spans.value: Da er informasjonen tydelig. Publikum trenger ikke å vite hvem som gjør alt arbeidet.

blocks.translation: Then the information is clear. The public does not need to know who does all the work.

spans.value: Marius now uses the two patterns for different jobs:

items.value: describe particular events in the reopening plan.
The workers are omitted because their identities are not relevant to visitors.

sections.title: A changed situation: opening a café

spans.value: The same grammar is useful when a new café is preparing to open.
A general customer procedure may use the s-passive:

en.value: Food is ordered at the counter.
Coffee is served from seven o’clock.
Tables are cleared after use.

spans.value: A particular preparation event may use

no.value: Det nye skiltet blir hengt opp i kveld.

en.value: The new sign will be put up this evening.
The coffee machine will be installed tomorrow.
The kitchen was inspected on Friday.

spans.value: Notice the transfer from the library context. The vocabulary has changed, but the meaning choice has not:

items.value: routine, procedure, or instruction → often s-passive
particular present, future, or past event → often bli-passive

prompt.value: Compare the two supplied library messages. Select one complete interpretation of what each passive puts in focus and why the employee need not be named.

options.text: Begge setningene setter den ansatte som utfører handlingen, i fokus; bordene og skiltet er bare bakgrunn. (Both sentences focus on the employee who acts; the tables and sign are only background.)
options.why: This reverses the information focus of a passive sentence.

options.text: «Bord ryddes etter bruk.» handler om én bestemt ansatt, mens «Det nye skiltet blir hengt opp i kveld.» er en generell rutine. Derfor må den ansatte navngis. (The first is about one particular employee, while the second is a general routine. Therefore the employee must be named.)
options.why: It confuses the routine with the particular event and wrongly makes the agent necessary.

options.text: «Bord ryddes etter bruk.» setter bordene og rutinen i fokus, mens «Det nye skiltet blir hengt opp i kveld.» setter den konkrete hendelsen med skiltet i fokus. Hvem som utfører handlingen, er ikke viktig. (The first focuses on tables and the routine; the second focuses on the particular sign event. The worker is not important.)
options.why: The affected thing or particular event is the focus, while the agent is irrelevant.

stem.value: Compare «Bord ryddes etter bruk.» and «Det nye skiltet blir hengt opp i kveld.» Which interpretation best explains what each passive puts in focus and why the worker is unnecessary?

prompt.value: Rewrite the procedural statement Ansatte rydder bord etter bruk. (Staff clear tables after use.) Put the affected item first, omit the worker, and remove the present-tense -r where needed to form the s-passive. Build exactly one complete Norwegian notice from the supplied tokens.

Recast two particular library updates as one complete sentence: the new sign will be put up this evening, and the door was repaired on Friday. Use blir/ble + past participle, place tense on bli, and omit the agents.

Build one complete library-reopening message from the tokens. Combine a recurring after-use procedure with a particular sign event this evening. Use an s-passive for the procedure, a bli-passive for the event, and omit the workers.

Rewrite the following practical notices in Norwegian. The named workers in the first two notices are irrelevant: put the affected item first, omit the worker, and choose a natural passive. Use an s-passive for the after-use routine and a bli-passive for the particular evening event. The worker in the third notice is relevant, so leave that notice unchanged. Return only the three resulting notices. 1. Renholderen rydder bord etter bruk. (The cleaner clears tables after use.) 2. Teknikeren henger opp det nye skiltet i kveld. (The technician puts up the new sign this evening.) 3. En bibliotekar møter deg ved inngangen klokka fem. (A librarian meets you at the entrance at five.)

payload.judge_prompt: Check the response against the task and report evidence for each criterion. The expected core rewrites are «Bord ryddes etter bruk.» and «Det nye skiltet blir hengt opp i kveld.», but accept equally natural Bokmål variants that preserve the same passive patterns and information focus. The relevant librarian must remain in the third notice.

criteria.instruction: Omits the irrelevant worker in the first two rewrites, puts the affected item first, and leaves the relevant librarian in the third notice.
Uses a natural s-passive for the after-use routine and a natural bli-passive for the evening event.

prompt.value: Revise Marius's draft public notice for the library reopening. Return only the revised Norwegian notice. Keep all four content points, remove irrelevant workers, put affected items or events first, use s-passives for recurring or instructional points, and use bli-passives for particular event updates. 1. Ansatte rydder bord etter bruk. (Staff clear tables after use.) 2. Renholderen vasker gulvet hver dag. (The cleaner washes the floor every day.) 3. Teknikeren henger opp det nye skiltet i kveld. (The technician puts up the new sign this evening.) 4. Vaktmesteren reparerte døren på fredag. (The caretaker repaired the door on Friday.)

payload.judge_prompt: Check all four content points against the task and report evidence for each criterion. Expected core forms are «Bord ryddes etter bruk.», «Gulvet vaskes hver dag.», «Det nye skiltet blir hengt opp i kveld.», and «Døren ble reparert på fredag.». Accept natural Bokmål variants only when they preserve all content cues, the requested passive distinction, and omission of irrelevant agents.

criteria.instruction: Recasts the first two recurring or instructional points as natural s-passives and preserves their cues such as etter bruk and hver dag.
Recasts the last two particular events as natural blir/ble + past participle forms and preserves their time cues.
Removes irrelevant workers and makes the affected items or events the focus throughout the revised notice.

prompt.value: Write two short Norwegian parts for a café opening: one public notice and one conversational internal update. In the public notice, state that napkins are collected at the counter every day and cups are cleared after use. Use s-passives for these recurring customer procedures. In the internal update, report that the new coffee machine will be installed tomorrow and the ventilation was inspected on Friday. Use bli-passives for these particular events. Omit workers when their identities do not matter. Use original café wording.

payload.judge_prompt: Check both parts against the task and report evidence for each criterion. Expected evidence is two public procedure sentences in -s and two internal event updates using blir/ble + past participle, with worker identities omitted. Accept natural Bokmål lexical variants that preserve the two communicative settings and passive prototypes, but do not accept a verbatim lesson sentence as the transfer response.

criteria.instruction: Uses natural s-passives for both recurring or direct-customer procedures in the public notice.
Uses natural blir/ble + past participle forms for both particular event updates in the internal message.
Omits worker identities where they do not matter and keeps the affected items or events in focus.

prompt.value: Respond in Norwegian. First state the practical tendency that distinguishes the two passive patterns. Then produce one Norwegian sentence for a recurring procedure with the exact cue hver dag and an s-passive, and one conversational report about a particular event happening now or already completed with a bli-passive and an explicit time cue. Omit an irrelevant agent in both sentences. Use original wording for a setting such as a café, office, or shop.

payload.judge_prompt: Check the response against the task and report evidence for each criterion. Accept concise natural Bokmål wording and different lexical frames, including either blir or ble for the particular event, when the time cue and event reading are clear. Do not require a verbatim model sentence.

criteria.instruction: States in Norwegian that s-passive is often used for routines, procedures, or instructions, while bli-passive is often used for particular events.
Provides one natural Bokmål s-passive sentence with hver dag, omitting an irrelevant agent and focusing the affected thing.
Provides one natural Bokmål bli-passive sentence for a current or completed particular event with an explicit time cue, omitting an irrelevant agent and focusing the affected event or thing.
